chunks: 5051 - Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from al-Asbagh ibn al-Asbagh, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Misri narrated to me from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah or from Burayd al-Ijli—the doubt is from Muhammad—who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A slave committed zina. He said: "He is to be lashed half of the hadd." I said: Then if he repeats it? He said: "Then he is struck the same as that." He said: I said: Then if he repeats it? He said: "No more than half of the hadd is added upon him."

He said: I said: Is stoning ever incumbent upon him for any of his acts? He said: "Yes, he is killed on the eighth [offense] if he does that eight times." He said: I said: What is the difference between him and the free man, when their act is one and the same? He said: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had mercy on him by not combining upon him the bond of slavery and the hadd of the free man." He said: Then he said: "And it is upon the Imam of the Muslims to pay his price to his master from the share of the riqab."

key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the leader vested with authority over Muslim legal administration
key_terms.حَدَّ الْحُرِّ: the legal punishment applied to a free person
key_terms.رِبْقَ الرِّقِّ: the bond or burden of slavery
key_terms.سَهْمِ الرِّقَابِ: the zakat allocation designated for freeing slaves
key_terms.نِصْفَ الْحَدِّ: half of the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a slave who commits zina in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling for a slave who commits zina: he receives half the hadd, and this does not increase beyond that amount upon repetition. If the offense is repeated eight times, he is killed on the eighth, and the Imam of the Muslims is to compensate the master from the zakat share designated for freeing slaves.
